metadata.title: Green Hydrogen in the EU: Investment, Regulation and Real Capacity 2024-2026

paragraphs.text: # Green Hydrogen in the EU: Investment, Regulation and Real Capacity 2024-2026

In 2024, the European Union recorded a 35% increase in installed electrolyser capacity for clean hydrogen, reaching a total of 1.2 GW of operational capacity. This jump is driven mainly by the funding mechanism of the European Hydrogen Bank.

According to a report by the International Energy Agency (IEA), the average production cost of green hydrogen in Europe fell to EUR 2.50 per kilogram at the end of 2024. This makes green hydrogen cheaper than hydrogen produced from natural gas.
The Renewable Energy Directive (RED III) requires industry in the member states to use at least 42% renewable fuels of non-biological origin (RFNBO) by 2030 and 60% by 2035.

Bulgaria has started building its first national hydrogen valley, "Zagore", near Stara Zagora with a budget of EUR 300 million, and the project has already been fully commissioned for commercial operation as of January 2025.

claims.original_text: reaching a total of 1.2 GW of operational capacity
claims.normalized_claim: Operational electrolyser capacity in the EU reached 1.2 GW by the end of 2024
claims.rationale: Installed operational capacity in the EU in 2024 is roughly 0.6 GW. The 1.2 GW figure includes planned or under-construction capacity, not plants actually operating at that date.
claims.recommended_edit: Replace “reaching a total of 1.2 GW of operational capacity” with “reaching about 580 MW of operational capacity, with more than 1.2 GW under construction”.
claims.editor_comment: Operational capacity is conflated with the total project pipeline.

evidence_links.finding: Installed operational electrolysis capacity in Europe stands at approx. 580 MW in 2024.

claims.original_text: This jump is driven mainly by the funding mechanism of the European Hydrogen Bank.
claims.normalized_claim: The European Hydrogen Bank provides key funding support for new EU projects
claims.rationale: The European Hydrogen Bank ran its first successful auction in 2024, awarding EUR 720 million from the Innovation Fund to 7 projects.

evidence_links.finding: Commission awards €720 million for 7 renewable hydrogen projects via the European Hydrogen Bank.

claims.original_text: the average production cost of green hydrogen in Europe fell to EUR 2.50 per kilogram at the end of 2024
claims.normalized_claim: The production cost of green hydrogen in Europe in 2024 is EUR 2.50/kg
claims.rationale: The actual levelised cost (LCOH) of green hydrogen in Europe in 2024 is between EUR 5.50 and 7.80/kg because of electricity prices and CAPEX inflation. EUR 2.50/kg is a long-term projection for 2030 and later.
claims.recommended_edit: Replace “fell to EUR 2.50 per kilogram” with “ranges between EUR 5.50 and 7.80 per kilogram, depending on electricity prices”.
claims.editor_comment: Understated by more than half compared with actual market levels.

evidence_links.finding: Levelised cost of renewable hydrogen in Europe in 2024 averages between 5.50 and 7.80 EUR/kg.

claims.original_text: This makes green hydrogen cheaper than hydrogen produced from natural gas.
claims.normalized_claim: Green hydrogen in Europe is cheaper than grey (fossil) hydrogen
claims.rationale: Grey hydrogen (from methane via SMR) cost about EUR 2.10-2.60/kg in the EU in 2024, which makes it significantly cheaper than green hydrogen (EUR 5.50/kg and above).
claims.recommended_edit: Replace the claim with: “However, without subsidies green hydrogen still costs about twice as much as hydrogen from natural gas.”
claims.editor_comment: Factually wrong comparison that is highly misleading.

evidence_links.finding: Fossil SMR hydrogen costs 2.10-2.60 EUR/kg compared to 5.50+ for renewable H2.

claims.original_text: requires industry in the member states to use at least 42% renewable fuels of non-biological origin (RFNBO) by 2030 and 60% by 2035
claims.normalized_claim: RED III requires a 42% RFNBO share in industry by 2030 and 60% by 2035
claims.rationale: Article 22a(1) of Directive (EU) 2023/2413 sets exactly these targets for hydrogen used in industry.

evidence_links.finding: RFNBO share in industry: at least 42% by 2030 and 60% by 2035.

claims.original_text: Bulgaria has started building its first national hydrogen valley, "Zagore", near Stara Zagora
claims.normalized_claim: The Zagore project near Stara Zagora is Bulgaria's first hydrogen valley
claims.rationale: The Hydrogen Valley Zagore project is the first hydrogen valley in Bulgaria registered and supported by the Clean Hydrogen Partnership.

evidence_links.finding: Officially awarded first Bulgarian Hydrogen Valley by the Clean Hydrogen Joint Undertaking.

claims.original_text: with a budget of EUR 300 million, and the project has already been fully commissioned for commercial operation as of January 2025
claims.normalized_claim: The Zagore hydrogen valley costs EUR 300 million and has been in commercial operation since January 2025
claims.rationale: The Clean Hydrogen Partnership grant is EUR 8.2 million and the planned investment for the initial phase is about EUR 16-20 million (not EUR 300 million). Implementation started in 2024-2025, and operation is expected to be phased in by 2028-2029.
claims.recommended_edit: Replace with: “with EU funding of EUR 8.2 million; pilot operation is expected to start in 2026-2027”.
claims.editor_comment: Budget scale is wrong and commercial operation is announced prematurely.

evidence_links.finding: Total project grant: EUR 8.2 million. Timeline: 2023-2028.
